What will be the output of the following pseudo-code?

```
Integer s = 0
for (i = 1 to 5)
  s = s + i * 2
end for
print s
```
explanation: The loop adds 2i for i = 1..5: 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 + 10 = 30. So s = 30 is printed.

What will be the output of the following pseudo-code?

```
Integer a = 12, b = 7
if (a mod 5 > b mod 5)
  print a - b
else
  print a + b
end if
```

Note: mod gives the remainder after division.
explanation: a mod 5 = 12 mod 5 = 2 and b mod 5 = 7 mod 5 = 2. The condition 2 > 2 is false, so the else branch runs and prints a + b = 12 + 7 = 19.

What will be the output of the following pseudo-code?

```
Integer a = 8, b = 3, c = 5
if (a > b and b > c)
  print 1
else if (a > c or c < b)
  if (a mod b == c mod b)
    print 2
  else
    print 3
  end if
else
  print 4
end if
```

Note: mod gives the remainder after division.
explanation: First condition: a > b is true but b > c (3 > 5) is false, so 'and' gives false. Second: a > c (8 > 5) is true, so 'or' gives true. Inner check: 8 mod 3 = 2 and 5 mod 3 = 2, equal, so 2 is printed.

What will be the output of the following pseudo-code?

```
Integer x = 0
for (i = 1 to 10)
  if (i mod 3 == 0)
    continue
  end if
  if (x > 20)
    break
  end if
  x = x + i
end for
print x
```

Note: continue skips to the next iteration; break exits the loop.
explanation: Multiples of 3 are skipped. x: i=1→1, i=2→3, i=4→7, i=5→12, i=7→19. At i=8, x = 19 is not > 20, so x = 27. i=9 is skipped. At i=10, x = 27 > 20, so the loop breaks. Output 27.

What will be the output of the following pseudo-code?

```
Integer f(Integer a, Integer b)
  Integer t = 0
  while (b > 0)
    if (b mod 2 == 1)
      t = t + a
    end if
    a = a * 2
    b = b / 2
  end while
  return t
end function

print f(6, 11) - f(11, 6)
```

Note: / is integer division and mod gives the remainder.
explanation: f is shift-and-add multiplication. f(6,11): b = 11,5,2,1 with a = 6,12,24,48; odd b adds 6+12+48 = 66. f(11,6): b = 6,3,1 with a = 11,22,44; odd b adds 22+44 = 66. Both equal 6 × 11, so 66 − 66 = 0.

What will be the output of the following pseudo-code?

```
Integer g(Integer n)
  Integer c = 0
  while (n > 0)
    n = n & (n - 1)
    c = c + 1
  end while
  return c
end function

print g(45) + g(64) * 10
```

Note: & is bitwise AND.
explanation: n & (n − 1) clears the lowest set bit, so g counts set bits. 45 = 101101 in binary has 4 set bits, so g(45) = 4. 64 = 1000000 has 1 set bit, so g(64) = 1. Output = 4 + 1 × 10 = 14.

What does this Python code print?
```
x = [1, 2, 3]
y = x
y.append(4)
print(len(x))
```
explanation: y = x copies the reference, not the list, so x and y name the same list. Appending 4 through y changes that list, so len(x) is 4.
